ideas.title: Student Journey Check
ideas.summary: For solo course creators and small training businesses on WordPress: a test student walks your course site every day and after every update, and tells you in plain words when login, lessons, quizzes, certificates or checkout break.

public.summary: A pretend student checks your online course every day and tells you the moment something your real students rely on stops working.
public.problem: You update a plugin, everything looks fine from your admin screen, and you move on. Days later a student emails to say they can't open the lesson they paid for, or their quiz results never appear, or the certificate page shows an error. By then other students have hit the same wall and quietly given up.
public.forWhom: Coaches, tutors, yoga and fitness teachers, and small training academies who sell courses from their own WordPress site.
benefits: Find out about a broken course before your students do
Know within minutes whether an update broke anything
See exactly which step failed, with a picture of what students saw
Spend less time answering 'I can't get in' emails
Keep selling while you fix it, instead of losing a week of sales

ideas.problemStatement: I updated the LMS plugin and my site looked fine to me, but my clients could not reach the courses they had bought, quiz results stopped showing, the certificate page errored for everyone, or every lesson video stopped playing. I only found out when students complained.
ideas.description: The owner enters the site URL, a dedicated test-student login, and the course and price they expect to see. On a daily schedule, and on demand right after an update, a headless browser walks a fixed student journey: log in, open the dashboard, open one lesson, confirm the video frame loads without a player error, open the course certificate page, and load the checkout page to compare the displayed price with the expected one. Each step is a pass or fail with a screenshot, and failures send one plain-language email ('Your student dashboard is covered by a popup since this morning'). Quiz submission is opt-in, against a dedicated test quiz, so the owner's real analytics stay clean. The first version supports Tutor LMS only, with known page paths, and adds LearnPress and LifterLMS after that.
ideas.targetCustomer: Solo course creators, coaches, and small training businesses (for example a dental training academy, a yoga teacher, a language school) who run Tutor LMS on their own WordPress site and maintain it themselves.
ideas.buyer: The business owner, on a personal or business card, from the same budget that pays for hosting and the LMS Pro licence.
ideas.whyNow: Tutor LMS shipped its 4.x line in August to October 2026, and the support forum shows a run of student-facing breakages after updates (login and admin dead after 4.0.7, dashboard blocked after 4.1.1, certificate pages broken on 4.x, quiz results not displaying), each found by the owner only after students complained.
ideas.founderFit: Pisan ships small React and Supabase web apps alone and teaches with browser automation and agentic coding tools, so a Playwright-based checker is squarely in his stack. As an instructor he knows the student journey (lesson, quiz, results, certificate) better than a generic uptime vendor does.

problemEvidence.author: ManageWP (GoDaddy)
problemEvidence.summary: Sells uptime monitoring at $1 per site per month (in 100-site bundles) and Safe Updates that require premium backup: agencies pay per site to avoid broken updates. Date is the fetch date; the page is undated.

competitors.name: Velprove
competitors.price: Free tier with 1 real-browser login monitor; $19 and $49 plans (from a vendor-written guide; pricing page not fetched)
competitors.gap: Checks that a test user can log in, which covers the worst case, but not lesson, video, quiz results, certificate or checkout price.

competitors.name: ManageWP Safe Updates
competitors.price: Requires premium backup; uptime monitor $1/site/month in 100-site bundles
competitors.gap: Agency tool; compares logged-out page screenshots around updates, not a logged-in student flow.

competitors.name: WP Engine Smart Plugin Manager
competitors.price: Reseller pricing 'as low as $2 per site'; list price unknown
competitors.gap: Visual regression on public pages with rollback, aimed at hosts and agencies; does not walk lessons, quizzes or certificates.

competitors.name: Checkly
competitors.price: Free tier; paid browser checks billed per 1k runs ($4.00 per 1k extra)
competitors.gap: Needs the owner to write Playwright scripts; built for developers, not a yoga teacher.

keyFeatures: Fixed Tutor LMS student journey with pass or fail per step and screenshots
Run-now button for right after a plugin update
Expected-price check on the checkout page
Plain-language failure email naming the broken step
Opt-in test quiz so real quiz analytics stay clean

features: Login, dashboard, one lesson, certificate page, checkout price
outOfScope: Video playback verification beyond detecting a player error frame
mvpScope.buildEstimate: 3 to 4 weeks, most of it on reliable selectors and the worker that runs the browsers

ideas.techStack: React + Vite + Tailwind front end, Supabase (auth, schedules, results, encrypted test credentials), a small Playwright worker on a cheap VM or container; no AI API.

pricing.rationale: Above the $1 to $2 per site agency tools because it walks a logged-in student flow, but well under the $19 Velprove starter tier; the reviewer judged even this hard to sell to owners who resent a $199/yr Pro licence.

ideas.revenueSketch: Estimate only: 150 sites x $9/month = $1,350 MRR. Assumes roughly 0.15% of Tutor LMS's 100,000 active installs convert, which is unproven.
ideas.distribution: A free one-off 'student journey check' page that anyone can run against their course site, linked from helpful answers to breakage threads on the Tutor LMS support forum (no promotion in threads, per forum rules) and from Tutor LMS Facebook groups; then a listing as a free helper plugin that points to the hosted checker.

validationTest.method: Build the free one-off check for Tutor LMS (login, dashboard, lesson, certificate, checkout price) and offer it to the posters of recent breakage threads and in two Tutor LMS owner groups. Ask everyone who runs it whether they want it daily for $9/month, and take pre-orders.
validationTest.successCriteria: At least 40 owners run the free check within 4 weeks, and at least 5 pre-pay for the daily plan.
validationTest.cost: About 1 week of build time and under $20 of hosting.

ideas.moat: Thin. A library of tested student-journey scripts per LMS and theme, and a record of which plugin versions broke which steps, which could become an 'is this update safe?' feed. It is easy to copy for one LMS.
compliance: Credentials: stores a low-privilege test-student password; encrypt at rest, never ask for admin or payment keys.
GDPR: screenshots may capture other students' names on leaderboards or forums; crop or blur, keep 14 days, and offer a data processing agreement to EU owners.
Site terms: the owner must authorise checks on their own site; rate-limit to avoid tripping security plugins.
Accessibility: the dashboard and emails must meet WCAG 2.2 AA.

risks.risk: Login CAPTCHAs (Turnstile, hCaptcha, Wordfence) block the test browser.
risks.mitigation: Document an allowlist for the test account or the worker's IP; detect and report 'blocked by CAPTCHA' as its own state.

risks.risk: Selectors break across themes and page builders, producing false alarms that make owners mute the alerts.
risks.mitigation: Support Tutor LMS default templates first, require two consecutive failures before alerting, and let the owner mark a step as not applicable.

risks.risk: Owners will not pay monthly because students' own emails already detect the worst breaks.
risks.mitigation: The validation test asks for pre-payment before the daily product is built.

risks.risk: A free real-browser login monitor (Velprove) already covers the most severe failure.
risks.mitigation: Compete only on the LMS steps that it does not check: lesson, certificate, results, price.

scoreRationale.pain: Five independent owners report student-facing breakage after Tutor updates in Aug to Oct 2026 (https://wordpress.org/support/topic/wp-admin-inaccessible-since-the-4-0-7-update/), but threads are low-volume, some are site-specific, and students report the worst breaks quickly.
scoreRationale.willingnessToPay: Agencies pay $1 to $2 per site for update safety (https://managewp.com/pricing), but these owners balk at a $199/yr Pro licence (https://tutorlms.com/pricing/) and treat monitoring as free.
scoreRationale.reachability: Owners are findable on the Tutor LMS support forum (https://wordpress.org/support/topic/tutor-lms-4-1-1-welcome-onboarding-popup-is-stuck-and-blocks-student-dashboard/), but forum rules forbid promotion and they arrive after the fix.
scoreRationale.competitiveGap: Velprove's free tier already runs a real-browser test-user login check (https://dev.to/velprove/definitive-wordpress-uptime-monitoring-guide-for-2026-48g4); only the lesson, results, certificate and price steps are uncovered.
scoreRationale.feasibility: Headless browsers per site, theme-dependent selectors, CAPTCHAs and cross-origin video frames make it fragile for one person to run (https://www.checklyhq.com/pricing/ shows the per-run cost of browser checks).
scoreRationale.complianceBurden: Only a low-privilege test password and screenshots are stored, no payment keys or admin access (https://wordpress.org/support/topic/certificate-builder-1-1-1-broken-on-tutor-4-x-nonce-error-critical-error/ shows the pages checked are ones every visitor sees).

review.findings: Reviewer rescored from 20 to 16. Pain 4->3: threads are low-volume, support called the popup and YouTube 153 cases site-specific or unreproducible, and students report hard breaks within hours. WTP 3->2: buyers resent $199/yr Tutor Pro; agency safe-update tools cost about $2 per site. Gap 3->2: Velprove's free tier includes one real-browser login monitor with a test subscriber account and names LMS sites as a fit. Feasibility 3->2: fragile selectors, Turnstile or hCaptcha on login, cross-origin video iframes, quiz submissions polluting analytics, and per-site browser ops. No rejection rule tripped; risk of drifting into per-site consulting. Reviewer's Velprove pricing came from a vendor-written dev.to guide, not the pricing page.

gateGap.closedBy: The validation test's pre-orders close the largest gap, willingness to pay: 5 owners pre-paying $9/month would lift WTP to 3, and 40 free runs that surface real breakages would support pain 4. Reaching 22 also needs a feasibility answer to CAPTCHAs and theme selectors, shown by the free check working on most of the sites that try it.

ideas.title: Misrepresentation Preflight
ideas.summary: For small online stores suspended, or afraid of being suspended, by Google Merchant Center for 'Misrepresentation': a cross-page consistency check that shows where the store contradicts itself before the owner spends a review attempt.

public.summary: Before you ask Google to look at your store again, see every place where your store tells shoppers two different things.
public.problem: Your Google Shopping account gets suspended for 'misrepresentation' and Google won't say what it found. You fix the footer, rewrite a policy, and ask for a review, and it comes back rejected again. Each rejection makes the next wait longer, and your ads may be at risk too.
public.forWhom: Owners of small online shops who sell through Google Shopping and do their own store admin.
benefits: Know what to fix before you spend your next review request
See where your contact details, shipping times or returns don't match from page to page
Get a dated record of what you fixed and when
Catch new contradictions after a theme or app change, before Google does

ideas.problemStatement: Google suspends the store for Misrepresentation without naming the cause; owners fix what forum replies suggest, burn review attempts, and stay suspended for months, often because small inconsistencies across Shopify, the feed, policies and business information pile up unseen.
ideas.description: The owner enters a store URL and optionally uploads the product feed export. The app crawls the public pages and compares what they say: business name, address, phone and email across footer, contact and policy pages; shipping and return windows across policy pages, product pages and the feed; price and availability across the product page, its JSON-LD and the feed; duplicate Product schema blocks; and risky claim words such as 'authorized' or 'official'. It returns a prioritized list of contradictions with the exact page and text, and keeps a dated re-check log the owner can use before requesting review. It does not promise reinstatement.
ideas.targetCustomer: Owners of small Shopify, WooCommerce and Wix stores (often sole proprietors) whose Google Merchant Center account is suspended or under 'website needs improvement' for Misrepresentation.
ideas.buyer: The store owner, on a personal or business card, out of the ad budget that the suspension has frozen.
ideas.whyNow: Forum threads from July to October 2026 show repeated suspensions and exhausted appeals, and at least five Shopify apps launched between March and October 2026 to chase the problem, which confirms the pain but also crowds the space.
ideas.founderFit: Pisan can ship a crawler-plus-report web app alone in days with his React/Flask stack, and the core is deterministic text and structured-data comparison rather than a paid AI call. His network is not in e-commerce, so distribution is self-serve through the Shopify community forum, which is the weakest part of the fit.

problemEvidence.author: unknown

competitors.name: AdNabu Misrepresentation Checker
competitors.gap: Free, works on any platform; reviewer found it checks business-name consistency but does not clearly compare shipping and return terms across pages and the feed.

competitors.name: Torhen GMC Rescue
competitors.gap: Shopify-only; flags feed price differences and writes appeal letters; launched 2026-10-12 with 0 reviews.

competitors.name: GMC Compliance Checker
competitors.gap: Shopify-only, product-policy focus; launched 2026-10-06 with 0 reviews.

keyFeatures: Cross-page comparison of business identity, shipping and returns text
Product page vs JSON-LD vs feed price and availability diff
Duplicate Product schema and risky-claim-word detection
Dated re-check log for review requests

features: URL crawl of up to 50 pages plus an uploaded feed CSV
Identity, shipping-window and return-window consistency report
Price and availability diff between page, JSON-LD and feed

ideas.techStack: React + Vite + Tailwind front end, Flask crawler with a parsing queue, Supabase for scan history; no paid AI API at runtime.

pricing.model: One-time pre-review scan with an optional monthly re-check
pricing.rationale: Below the $24.99-$29/month Shopify apps and the EUR 99 manual audit, because free tiers exist and buyers are distressed small stores.

ideas.revenueSketch: Estimate only: 40 one-time scans a month at $29 plus 60 monthly subscribers at $9 is about $1,700/month. Assumes a non-Shopify niche the Shopify-only apps miss; unproven.
ideas.distribution: Answer Misrepresentation threads in the Shopify Community and Google Merchant Center Community with a free one-page cross-check, then the WooCommerce and Wix forums where the Shopify-only apps cannot reach.

validationTest.method: Publish a free single-scan cross-page check (identity, shipping, returns) on a landing page with a $29 'full report and re-check log' button; post it once in 3 active Misrepresentation threads and the WooCommerce forum.
validationTest.successCriteria: At least 5 paid $29 reports within 30 days, with at least 2 from non-Shopify stores, and at least 3 of the first 20 free scans surfacing a contradiction the owner did not know about.
validationTest.cost: About 1 week of build and $0 to $20 in hosting.

ideas.moat: Weak. The comparison logic is copyable; the only defensible pieces are non-Shopify coverage and an accumulating library of contradiction patterns tied to outcomes owners report back.
compliance: Crawls public third-party pages: respect robots.txt and rate limits
Stores owner-uploaded feed files: delete after 30 days, no customer PII
Marketing must not imply guaranteed reinstatement (refund and consumer-protection risk)

risks.risk: Free tools and five new Shopify apps already cover most checks
risks.mitigation: Lead with non-Shopify stores and the cross-page shipping/returns comparison the reviewer found no free tool doing; kill if the validation test shows no paid conversions.

risks.risk: Many suspensions have no on-site cause a tool can find
risks.mitigation: Say so plainly in the report and offer a refund when the scan finds nothing.

risks.risk: Forums are saturated with vendor pitches, so posts read as spam
risks.mitigation: Answer specific threads with a concrete finding from the free scan rather than a link drop.

scoreRationale.pain: Three independent owners describe repeated or months-long suspensions in Jul-Oct 2026 (https://community.shopify.com/t/third-merchant-center-suspended-for-misrepresentation-any-realistic-chance-and-how-do-i-protect-google-ads/698844), but much of the pain is Google's opacity, which no tool can fix.
scoreRationale.willingnessToPay: The only spend seen is sellers offering a EUR 99 audit (https://community.shopify.com/t/google-merchant-center-misrepresentation-pre-review-shopify-audit-99/668558) and a VA job posting (https://www.onlinejobs.ph/jobseekers/job/1616633); the Shopify apps charging $19.99-$29/month all show 0 reviews (https://apps.shopify.com/torhen-gmc-rescue).
scoreRationale.reachability: Owners post publicly in the Shopify Community (https://community.shopify.com/t/google-merchant-center-misrepresentation-suspension-for-8-months-appeals-exhausted-any-similar-cases/666324), but those threads are crowded with service pitches and free audit offers (https://community.shopify.com/t/free-merchant-center-misrepresentation-audit-first-5-stores/690116).
scoreRationale.competitiveGap: A free platform-agnostic checker (https://adnabu.com/free-tools/misrepresentation-checker) plus at least five Shopify apps with free tiers (https://apps.shopify.com/gmc-compliance-checker-1) cover most checks; only cross-page shipping and returns comparison looked uncovered.
scoreRationale.feasibility: A URL crawler and diff report fit one person, but checkout crawling, bot protection and Google's unstated criteria (https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/6150127) make the full scope fragile.
scoreRationale.complianceBurden: No customer PII, but it crawls third-party sites, stores feed files and must avoid implied reinstatement claims (https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/6150127).

review.findings: Reviewer rescored from 22 to 17, calling it borderline kill. Pain 5->4: real, but many suspensions (8 months, appeals exhausted) have no fixable on-site cause. WTP 3->2: the EUR 99 audit and the OnlineJobs posting are seller and VA signals, not owners buying a scan; LisaR's earlier suspension followed a paid 'specialist'. Gap 2->1: AdNabu's free checker works on any platform and checks business-name consistency; Torhen, ShopSniff and others (GMC Scout, Selofy, FeedSiren, GMC Guard per search, unfetched) cover feed price checks and appeal letters. Feasibility 4->3: checkout crawling behind bot protection and copied-text detection are hard without paid services, so both were cut from the MVP. Compliance 5->4. Only gap found: no free tool comparing shipping and return terms in the feed against live policy pages.

gateGap.closedBy: The validation test's $29 paid-report button closes the largest gap, willingness to pay: 5 paid reports in 30 days, 2 of them from non-Shopify stores, would support WTP 3 and a competitiveGap of 2 for the non-Shopify niche. Even then the total would sit near 19, so a promotion to validated also needs a free-scan hit rate showing the cross-page check finds contradictions the existing tools miss.

ideas.title: Popup Check
ideas.summary: For small online-store owners: triggers every popup, age gate, cookie banner and chat bubble on the site and checks each one with the keyboard and a screen-reader view, then produces a dated report.

public.summary: Find out whether the popups on your store lock out shoppers who use a keyboard or a screen reader, before someone else finds out for you.
public.problem: You add an email sign-up popup, an age gate or a cookie banner, and it looks fine to you. To a shopper using a screen reader it can be a wall: focus never reaches it, the close button has no name, and Escape does nothing. Popups are among the failures that show up in website accessibility demand letters, and the free checkers mostly test the page as it looks before the popup appears.
public.forWhom: Owners of small online shops who run their own store and add popups, banners and chat widgets through apps.
benefits: See which of your popups a keyboard or screen-reader user cannot close or use
Get plain instructions, or a note that the popup app itself needs replacing
Keep a dated record of what you checked and changed
Get re-checked automatically after you add or change an app

ideas.problemStatement: Store owners install popup, age-gate, cookie and chat apps they cannot edit; those overlays often trap or skip keyboard focus and lack accessible names, and one owner reports being sued over a popup that did not work with screen readers.
ideas.description: Popup Check opens the store in a headless browser, finds the overlays (email capture, spin-to-win, age gates, cookie banners, chat launchers) and triggers each one by timer, scroll, exit intent and first-visit state. For each overlay it runs scripted keyboard tests (does focus move in, is it trapped while open, does Escape close it, does focus return, does the close control have an accessible name) plus axe-core on the open state. The report names the app behind each overlay where it can, says whether the fix is a setting or a different app, and keeps a dated history. A weekly re-check flags new overlays after an app install. The report is worded as test results, never as a compliance certificate.
ideas.targetCustomer: Owners and solo operators of small online stores on Shopify, WordPress/WooCommerce or Squarespace who add marketing popups and banners through apps.
ideas.buyer: The store owner, on a personal or business card, from the marketing or website budget.
ideas.whyNow: ADA website demand letters to small stores continue in 2026, and the store-owner complaint here is dated 2026-05-12. Free scanners test the page at load; the one modal-dialog guided test found is in paid axe DevTools Pro.
ideas.founderFit: Pisan works in accessibility and can build Playwright and axe-core tooling alone; the scripted keyboard checks are the kind of thing he already teaches. He has no special channel into store owners, so distribution is self-serve.

problemEvidence.author: Boyt Harness
problemEvidence.summary: A US store gives Shopify Forms (766 reviews) one star: 'We got sued because the pop up is not compliment for people with disablilities that require screen readers.' It is the only accessibility complaint among that app's 1 and 2 star reviews.

competitors.name: axe DevTools Pro (Deque), Modal Dialog guided test
competitors.gap: Checks focus trapping, Escape and focus return, but it is a manual guided test in a developer tool, not an automated popup trigger for store owners.

competitors.name: Remedy (iTechVista)
competitors.price: Free plan available; paid plans unknown
competitors.gap: Scans the storefront with axe-core and keeps a dated record, but its listing does not mention triggering or testing overlays; Shopify only, launched 2026-08-21, 0 reviews.

competitors.name: Shopify Forms
competitors.gap: The popup builder itself; a merchant cannot edit its markup, so the only fix is a setting or a different app.

keyFeatures: Finds and triggers popups, age gates, cookie banners and chat launchers
Scripted keyboard tests: focus in, focus trap, Escape, focus return, close-button name
axe-core run on each overlay's open state
Names the app behind each overlay and whether the fix is a setting or a swap
Dated report history and weekly re-check

features: One-URL scan that triggers timer and scroll popups and the first-visit state
Five keyboard checks plus axe-core on each open overlay
Dated PDF and web report with plain-language fixes
outOfScope: Automatic fixes or a script injected into the store

ideas.techStack: React + Vite, Flask or Node worker running Playwright and axe-core, Supabase for accounts and report history; no paid API at runtime.

pricing.model: per-store subscription, with a one-off report
pricing.pricePoint: $9/month, or $29 for a single dated report
pricing.rationale: Below overlay subscriptions and far below a remediation engagement; the one-off report suits owners who just received a letter. Willingness to pay is unproven.

ideas.revenueSketch: Estimate: 150 stores x $9/month = $1,350 MRR plus 20 one-off reports a month x $29 = $580. Assumes self-serve conversion that has not been tested.
ideas.distribution: A free one-popup check as the funnel, posted in the Shopify Community accessibility threads and WordPress accessibility forums; then the WordPress plugin directory as a thin connector.

validationTest.method: Build a one-URL free check that tests a single popup, and run it on 100 small stores found through Shopify Community and WordPress.org showcase posts to measure the failure rate. Offer the $29 dated report on the results page.
validationTest.successCriteria: At least 30 of 100 stores have a popup that fails a keyboard check, and at least 5 owners buy the $29 report within 30 days.
validationTest.cost: About 1 week of build and $0 to $20 of hosting.

ideas.moat: Weak. The reliable triggering of overlays and a library of known popup apps with their fix-or-swap advice is the only part that is hard to copy, and a scanner vendor could add it.
compliance: Accessibility: the report must be worded as test results, not a statement of ADA or WCAG compliance; the FTC fined an overlay vendor over compliance claims.
Privacy: scans public pages only; stores no shopper data.

risks.risk: A popup-only report does not settle a demand letter, which cites many failures, so owners may not pay for it.
risks.mitigation: Position it as prevention when adding apps, and price the one-off report low; test willingness to pay before building the weekly plan.

risks.risk: Popups fire on exit intent, timers, scroll or once per visitor, and bot protection blocks headless browsers, so triggering is unreliable and false positives are likely.
risks.mitigation: Start with timer, scroll and first-visit triggers only, and show the owner a screenshot of each overlay found so they can confirm it.

risks.risk: Merchants cannot fix third-party popup markup.
risks.mitigation: Make 'switch to this app or setting' a first-class result, backed by a list of popup apps that passed.

scoreRationale.pain: One dated store-owner complaint of being sued over a popup (https://apps.shopify.com/shopify-forms/reviews?ratings%5B%5D=1&ratings%5B%5D=2&sort_by=newest); the 2026 forum replies on ADA threads are mostly vendors, so this is capped at 3.
scoreRationale.willingnessToPay: No payment evidence for popup testing specifically; the one adjacent paid tool is axe DevTools Pro (https://docs.deque.com/devtools-for-web/4/en/devtools-igt-modal-dialog), sold to developers, not owners.
scoreRationale.reachability: Self-serve only: Shopify Community and WordPress forums, with no network advantage (https://apps.shopify.com/remedy-accessibility shows the same channel is already being worked).
scoreRationale.competitiveGap: No free tool found that triggers overlays and runs keyboard tests on them; Deque's guided test is manual and paid (https://docs.deque.com/devtools-for-web/4/en/devtools-igt-modal-dialog).
scoreRationale.feasibility: Reliable popup triggering across apps and bot protection is hard for one person, per review (https://apps.shopify.com/remedy-accessibility scans at load only).
scoreRationale.complianceBurden: Public pages only, but compliance-claim wording carries liability (https://apps.shopify.com/shopify-forms/reviews?ratings%5B%5D=1&ratings%5B%5D=2&sort_by=newest).

review.findings: Reviewer rescored from 20 to 17. No free tool was found that triggers and tests popups (gap stays 3; Deque's Modal Dialog guided test is in paid axe DevTools Pro, and Remedy's listing does not mention overlays). Pain 3: the Boyt Harness review is real but is the only accessibility complaint among Shopify Forms' 1-2 star reviews, and the 2026 replies in Shopify Community ADA threads 232788 and 230778 come from vendor accounts, so they were dropped as evidence. WTP 3->2: a popup-only report does not settle a demand letter, and money after a letter goes to lawyers. Reachability 4->3. Feasibility 3->2: exit-intent, timer and once-per-visitor triggers, bot protection and false positives. Compliance 5->4: the FTC's action against an overlay vendor means reports must not imply compliance.

gateGap.closedBy: The validation test's free one-popup check on 100 stores closes the evidence and pain gaps (a 30% failure rate plus owner replies would be new, dated evidence), and the $29 report offer closes willingness to pay: 5 paid reports in 30 days would support WTP 3. Promotion to validated would still need a second independent owner complaint and a total of 22.

watchlist.title: Cross-course content maintenance for Canvas design teams (bulk find, preview, replace and rollback for vendor-driven breakage)
watchlist.targetCustomer: Instructional designers and LMS admin teams who maintain content across dozens to thousands of Canvas courses.
watchlist.problemStatement: Vendor-side changes keep breaking content across many courses at once: Canvas's silent 2026-10-07 change to enhanceable_content tabs, Community guide links moving from /t5/ to /en/kb/, and LTI 1.3 migrations that leave embedded assignment links saying 'deleted'. Teams fix pages one at a time or with shared Tampermonkey scripts.
watchlist.missedGate: competitiveGap 2: Atomic Search already sells account-wide Find & Replace for Canvas, and free community userscripts cover bulk search and link conversion; total below 22.

watchlist.title: ADA demand-letter remediation ledger for small Shopify and WordPress stores
watchlist.targetCustomer: Small online store owners who have received an ADA website demand letter or lawsuit
watchlist.problemStatement: Owners who are served do not know where to start, get pitched overlays, and have no dated record of good-faith fixes mapped to the allegations.
watchlist.missedGate: No complaint dated within 180 days (the served owners posted in 2023 to 2025); competitiveGap 2 against remediation vendors and free axe/WAVE. 2026-11-03 extra run: a store owner's 2026-05-12 Shopify Forms review says they were sued over a popup (within 180 days), but Remedy (free plan, launched 2026-08-21) now keeps a dated accessibility record, so competitiveGap stays 2.

watchlist.title: Agent Exposure Audit for asynchronous online programs
watchlist.targetCustomer: Online program directors and instructional designers running asynchronous courses where proctoring is not feasible.
watchlist.problemStatement: Agentic browsers and cheap bots now complete Canvas New Quizzes and whole courses; quiz logs cannot prove it, and programs do not know which of their assessments an agent can finish unaided.
watchlist.missedGate: willingnessToPay 3 and competitiveGap 3 (Cursive sells LMS agent detection; the existing Assignment Stress Test idea covers testing assignments against AI); only one fetched item is within 90 days; total below 22. 2026-11-01: the CSU TILT page confirms agents complete Canvas quizzes but is undated and recommends the LockDown Browser campuses already license.

watchlist.title: Attempt-First Feedback Desk (AI first-pass feedback on ungraded practice with escalation to TAs)
watchlist.targetCustomer: Instructors of large CS and STEM courses who are moving homework to completion credit because of AI and have no grader budget.
watchlist.problemStatement: Homework is being de-graded, but instructors still want students to practice and get feedback; there is no grader budget, and students who used to come to office hours now go to general-purpose AI.
watchlist.missedGate: willingnessToPay 2 (instructors cite no grader budget) and competitiveGap 2 (CS50 Duck, PingPong, Gradescope AI features); risks being an AI wrapper.

watchlist.title: Alternative-grading layer for Canvas and autograders
watchlist.targetCustomer: CS and STEM instructors using specifications, standards-based or mastery grading on Canvas with PrairieLearn or Gradescope.
watchlist.problemStatement: LMSs and autograders only understand points, so instructors fake standards-based grades with zero-point assessments, hacky scripts and spreadsheets to handle learning targets, resubmission tokens and letter-grade bundles.
watchlist.missedGate: pain 3 (one GitHub RFC with 2 thumbs-up plus a position paper); total below 22.

watchlist.title: Course LLM key broker
watchlist.targetCustomer: Instructors teaching courses that use LLM APIs or coding agents without a campus AI gateway.
watchlist.problemStatement: Instructors need per-student capped API keys with model allowlists and term-end revocation; today they share keys, script OpenRouter or LiteLLM, or make students pay, and student keys leak.
watchlist.missedGate: pain 3 and willingnessToPay 2; campus gateways, Standard Compute, Anthropic per-user spend limits and OpenAI project limits are closing the gap.

watchlist.title: Health-page tracker audit for small health and wellness practices (HIPAA, Washington MHMDA)
watchlist.targetCustomer: Therapists, clinics, med spas and wellness shops with booking or intake pages
watchlist.problemStatement: Third-party widgets and pixels send page URLs and IPs from health-intent pages, and vendors will not sign a BAA.
watchlist.missedGate: Only 1 complaint (pain 3); Sift Health already sells this at $39/month draft pricing.

watchlist.title: AI shopping-agent readiness check for small Shopify stores (duplicate Product JSON-LD, availability and rating signals agents read)
watchlist.targetCustomer: Small Shopify merchants whose products AI assistants describe wrongly or as out of stock.
watchlist.problemStatement: ChatGPT and other agents report products as out of stock or with invented specs because of duplicate or stale Product schema, missing aggregateRating, and Shopify Catalog entries that disagree with the product page.
watchlist.missedGate: competitiveGap 1 (Botfound, FoundGPT and several free checkers already posted in the forum); willingnessToPay 2; total below 22. Not reviewed.

runNotes.caveats: No candidate cleared the gate. The strongest pain cluster (payments that never became enrollments or bookings, 6 owner threads from Aug to Oct 2026) was killed twice in review: once as an API-connected monitor (17) and once as a browser-only CSV check (16). Student Journey Check ships as provisional at 16, after review cut it from 20, chiefly because a free real-browser login monitor exists and buyers resent even a $199/yr licence. The Velprove pricing comes from a vendor-written guide, not a fetched pricing page. The ManageWP evidence date is the fetch date. The TPT source (B1) yielded only an undated $16 spend signal. The C10 change events (ThriveCart Learn retiring at the end of 2026, Thinkific's 10% rise, Kajabi's January rise) are each served by free vendor migrations. Watchlist searches found no new fetched evidence, so all 7 entries carry forward unchanged. Extra run (random sources A13 A5 B9 C4 C2): added idea 2, Misrepresentation Preflight, as provisional at 17 after review cut it from 22; the next candidate, Lead Form Watch, was reviewed and killed at 15. A5 Stack Exchange and C2 yielded no small-business signal (OpenAlex returned 429; arXiv worked). B9: Upwork 403s and Contra is a JS shell, but the freelancer.com public projects API returned dated listings via curl, though its query filter barely narrows results. C4 HigherEdJobs returned a stub, so C4 came from a web search on GMC specialist postings. A search snippet claimed GMC Compliance Checker had 201 reviews; its fetched page shows 0. Extra run (random sources A2 A4 B12 C1 C11): added idea 3, Popup Check, as provisional at 17 after review cut it from 20. Three higher candidates were reviewed and killed (Trusted Stocktake 23 to 17, PO Pack 20 to 16, Subscriber Desk 19 to 12), each because a free tool or a new Shopify API already covers it. A4 GitHub search returned 422 and was substituted with A13 (community.shopify.com); A2 Open edX, C1 and C11 produced no small-business signal. The Shopify App Store search page returns nothing, but app and review pages work with curl. The day now has three Multi-week ideas and no Weekend MVP, so the complexity-mix constraint is not met: no Weekend MVP candidate survived review.
